introduction: This spec adds per-phase tool-call and byte counters to agentrun.Result, the envelope's usage.phases[] and the phase_end event so that navigation improvements can be measured, and adds a relevant_files field to submit_prd so that spec generation phases after the PRD start from the files the PRD phase found relevant instead of rediscovering them.

glossary.Observer: The agentrun.Observer interface that receives phase progress events; implemented by toolio.Progress and test observers.
glossary.PhaseEndEvent: The JSONL event emitted when a model phase ends, defined in internal/toolio/events.go.
glossary.PhaseInfo: The per-phase cost record in the envelope's usage.phases[], defined in internal/toolio/envelope.go.
glossary.envelope: The single JSON object every agent-fox tool writes to stdout, defined by toolio.Envelope.
glossary.phase: One model-facing step of a pipeline, driven by agentrun.Runner.Run. Each phase is a fresh agent with its own system prompt, user prompt, tools and terminating tool.
glossary.relevant_files: An optional array on submit_prd listing repository files the PRD phase read and found important for later generation phases.
glossary.split: A run where the PRD phase reports the input as more than one spec's worth of work, producing multiple packages from a single input.

requirements.title: Tool-call and byte counters on agentrun.Result
requirements.rationale: Without per-tool call counts and byte volumes on the Result, navigation improvements cannot be measured from the envelope or event stream.

criteria.action: carry a ToolCalls field of type map[string]int that counts the number of calls to each tool by name, including blocked calls
carry a ToolResultBytes field of type map[string]int64 that sums the byte length of Content.Text() of each ToolResultMessage by tool name
count ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes in the same event-processing path (the trace method) that already counts ToolErrors and Blocked, on every phase of every tool, whether or not --verbose is set

criteria.condition: a tool call is blocked by the authorization guard
criteria.action: increment ToolCalls for that tool name but not increment ToolResultBytes, because the result is the guard's refusal message already counted as a tool error

criteria.condition: a tool call returns an error result that is not a guard refusal
criteria.action: increment both ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes for that tool name, using the byte length of the error text the model sees
for any phase that made zero tool calls, report ToolCalls as nil and ToolResultBytes as nil rather than empty maps

requirements.title: Tool-call counts in toolio.PhaseInfo
requirements.rationale: The envelope's usage.phases[] is the durable record of a run; without tool-call counts there, a caller must parse individual tool_call events to measure navigation.

criteria.action: carry a ToolCalls field of type map[string]int with JSON tag "tool_calls,omitempty" and trust classification fact
carry a ToolResultBytes field of type map[string]int64 with JSON tag "tool_result_bytes,omitempty" and trust classification fact
copy ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes from agentrun.Result into the PhaseInfo it returns
bump SchemaVersion from "3.0.0" to "3.1.0" and add a changelog line in docs/cli.md describing the addition of tool_calls and tool_result_bytes to usage.phases[] and relevant_files to the spec result

requirements.title: Tool-call counts in the phase_end event
requirements.rationale: A caller watching the event stream should see per-tool counts without waiting for the envelope.

criteria.action: carry a ToolCalls field of type map[string]int with JSON tag "tool_calls,omitempty"
accept a toolCalls map[string]int parameter and set it on the returned PhaseEndEvent
accept a toolCalls map[string]int parameter in its signature, and every implementation of Observer (toolio.Progress and test observers in internal/agentrun/hooks_test.go) shall be updated to match
pass the toolCalls parameter through to newPhaseEndEvent when emitting the phase_end event
pass the Result's ToolCalls map to Observer.PhaseEnd in the call that follows the run body
not carry ToolResultBytes, keeping the event compact; byte counts are available only in the envelope's usage.phases[]

requirements.title: submit_prd gains relevant_files
requirements.rationale: Without a relevant_files field, every generation phase rediscovers the files the PRD phase already identified, wasting turns on navigation.

criteria.action: include an optional relevant_files array of objects, each with a required path (string) and a required why (string), described to the model as 'the files a later phase should read first to write requirements, tests and tasks for this PRD'
enforce a maxItems of 30 on the relevant_files array in the schema definition, so the model sees the limit before it calls
carry a RelevantFiles field of type []RelevantFile where RelevantFile is struct { Path string; Why string }
store the validated relevant_files alongside the rest of the PRD when the submission is accepted

requirements.title: Path validation on relevant_files
requirements.rationale: A bad path costs one turn now rather than a wrong task later, matching the contract issuetriage's citation check uses.

criteria.condition: submit_prd is called with a relevant_files array
criteria.action: resolve every path with tools.Workspace.Resolve, check that it exists with os.Stat, and verify it is a regular file (not a directory)

criteria.condition: one or more paths in relevant_files fail resolution, do not exist, or are directories
criteria.action: reject the submission with a tool error naming each bad path, using the same error-result pattern as the existing specNameRE, empty-title and missing-intent checks
criteria.contract: core.ErrResult with code "invalid_relevant_files" and a message listing every bad path

criteria.condition: submit_prd is called without relevant_files or with an empty array
criteria.action: accept the submission without path validation, storing an empty or nil RelevantFiles on the PRD

requirements.title: Relevant-files block in generation and architecture prompts
requirements.rationale: Injecting the PRD phase's file list into later phases gives them a head start on navigation without sharing transcripts.

criteria.condition: the PRD phase supplied a non-empty relevant_files list
criteria.action: include a '## Files the PRD phase found relevant' block in the user prompt of each generation phase (generate:requirements, generate:test_spec, generate:tasks) and the optional architecture phase, placed after the landscape and steering blocks and before the prior-artifacts block
render each entry as '- `<path>` — <why>' and introduce the block with text stating it is the previous phase's notes, not instructions

criteria.condition: the PRD phase did not supply relevant_files (the field was omitted or the array was empty)
criteria.action: omit the relevant-files block entirely, producing a prompt byte-identical to what it would be without this change
carry the relevant_files list so that generationUserPrompt and the architecture prompt builder can access it

requirements.title: Relevant files on a split
requirements.rationale: Each scope's PRD phase reads different files; mixing them would mislead later phases.

criteria.condition: the input is split into multiple scopes
criteria.action: pass each scope's own PRD phase's relevant_files list to only that scope's generation and architecture phases, not to other scopes' phases
not carry relevant_files from a previous scope; the splitContext does not carry it across scopes

requirements.title: Relevant files in the envelope
requirements.rationale: The envelope is the durable record of a run; including relevant_files lets a caller see what the PRD phase identified without re-reading the events.

criteria.action: carry a RelevantFiles field with JSON tag "relevant_files,omitempty" and trust classification model (the why field is model text), populated from the PRD phase's output

criteria.condition: the input is split into multiple scopes
criteria.action: populate each Package in FollowOnSpecs with its own scope's relevant_files list
not persist relevant_files inside the spec package directory; it lives only in the envelope and the run-time pipeline

criteria.condition: a re-run continues from an existing PRD (the PRD phase does not run because a split plan exists)
criteria.action: run the later phases without the relevant-files block and emit a low-severity warning with code relevant_files_unavailable
declare a WarnRelevantFilesUnavailable constant with value "relevant_files_unavailable" and stage "prd" in the warnStages table, following the existing pattern

requirements.title: Navigation baseline procedure and tables in docs/development.md
requirements.rationale: Without a recorded baseline, the effect of later navigation changes (repository map, symbol tools, indexed search) cannot be measured in review.

criteria.action: contain a 'Navigation baseline' section with a procedure for running a fixed set of inputs per tool against this repository with --dry-run: issue (two inputs: a stack trace, a prose report), fix (two inputs naming a seeded defect), spec (three inputs), and impl (one small fixed spec package of at least three tasks)
contain one table per tool recording the per-phase tool_calls from those baseline runs
contain a note that the tables are regenerated by hand whenever a navigation change ships, and that no live-model run enters make test

execution_paths.title: A spec run reports per-phase tool-call counts in the envelope and event stream

steps.action: runs `spec <input>` against a repository
drives the PRD phase; the trace method counts every tool call and its result bytes in ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes on the Result
calls Observer.PhaseEnd with the Result's ToolCalls map; Progress emits a phase_end event carrying tool_calls
copies ToolCalls and ToolResultBytes from the Result into a PhaseInfo
records the PhaseInfo in the envelope's usage.phases[]
repeats the above for each generation phase (requirements, test_spec, tasks)
assembles the envelope with usage.phases[] carrying tool_calls and tool_result_bytes for every phase
reads the envelope's usage.phases[].tool_calls to see how many calls each phase made to each tool

execution_paths.title: A spec run passes relevant_files from the PRD phase to generation phases

steps.action: runs `spec <input>` against a repository
calls submit_prd with a relevant_files array listing files it read and found important
validates each path with Workspace.Resolve and os.Stat, accepts the submission, and stores RelevantFiles on the PRD
passes the PRD's RelevantFiles to each artifactRequest
renders a '## Files the PRD phase found relevant' block in the user prompt, after landscape and steering, before prior artifacts
reads the relevant-files block and starts from those files instead of rediscovering them
populates Package.RelevantFiles in the envelope result from the PRD's output

execution_paths.title: A resumed split run warns about unavailable relevant files

steps.action: runs `spec <input>` on an input whose split plan already exists on disk (a previous run was interrupted)
finds the split plan and skips the PRD phase for already-written scopes
detects that no relevant_files list is available for the resumed scope and emits a low-severity warning with code relevant_files_unavailable
omits the relevant-files block from the generation prompts for the resumed scope
sees the warning in the envelope's warnings[] array

execution_paths.title: submit_prd rejects invalid paths in relevant_files

steps.action: calls submit_prd with a relevant_files array containing a path that does not exist
resolves the path, finds it does not exist, and returns an error result with code invalid_relevant_files naming the bad path
receives the error, corrects the path, and resubmits
